correctness.rationale: For the first n arrivals all received bundles are singletons or empty, hence EF1. The first low-tier recipient j is unenvied: any other low-tier recipient i was unassigned when j received g_j and would have been preferred by the high-first rule if v_i(g_j)=h_i; so v_i(g_j)=ell_i=v_i(g_i). Any high-own agent i has v_i(g_i)=h_i>=v_i(g_j). If no low recipient exists every agent owns a high-valued good. Therefore give the last good to an unenvied anchor and remove only that last good for every other agent; pairwise singleton comparisons are trivially EF1. The proof covers all n and positive real tiers. Exact-integer checker reconstructed the rule and passed 3,908,208 instances and 21,778,368 prefix comparisons, which are corroboration rather than infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Direct comparison of exact hypotheses and conclusions against the complete relevant portions of five primary research PDFs, prior published research records, and accessible previous claims found no statement implying a universal, deterministic, zero-buffer, prefixwise EF1 guarantee for arbitrary positive personalized two-tier goods at the first surplus horizon. Choi--Li explicitly leave the unrestricted two-valued temporal EF1 case unresolved; Wang--Wei exact n-agent theorem assumes a strictly narrower homogeneous-agent class; the buffer paper requires deferred allocation. value.rationale: The horizon n+1 is the first meaningful online EF1 step beyond the trivial one-good-per-agent regime; it is the exact same supply threshold appearing in strong unrestricted negative results. The structural universally-unenvied anchor and simple high-first algorithm solve this motivated positive two-tier boundary for any number of heterogeneous agents without buffering, frequencies, or future order. The explicit two-agent obstruction to naive first-phase placement shows the preference-aware choice matters. The result is not just a routine table computation and has concrete interpretation for irreversible one-unit-surplus allocation.
